summary: Snapshot-affinity persistence during staggered canary causes subset of tenants to hit degraded fallback
description: Issue summary: During a staged canary with staggered weight shifts and snapshot replay, a subset (~8-12%) of tenant requests remained bound to the previous model variant (legacy/degraded) despite the control-plane indicating successful commit to the new variant. Impact: Customers at DataStream Labs reported increased inference latency (~200-500ms) and lower output quality on streaming endpoints for affected sessions. Scope: Observed in us-east-1 on Dedicated fleet for routes with cookie-based session affinity and prewarm snapshots enabled.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Create a rollout for route /v1/chat from redwood/open-7b-v2 -> redwood/align-13b with staged weights: 5% -> 25% -> 60% over 30m.
2) Enable prewarm snapshot mirror and cookie affinity with path / and domain datastream.example.
3) Simulate production-like client reconnects that reuse keep-alive but occasionally re-NEGOTIATE streams.
4) Observe that ~10% of sessions continue to be served by legacy variant after the 25% and 60% steps complete.
Expected: Affinity should bind to the current cohort based on the latest snapshot and model pin. Actual: Persistent binding to previous variant until cache TTL expiry or token rotation.
Note: Reproduction is intermittent and appears correlated with quick successive weight adjustments and edge-side memoization of route fingerprints.

investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: edge memoization combined with cookie path/domain normalization created stale fingerprint that continued to direct traffic to legacy variant despite control-plane snapshot commit.
Evidence: edge logs show memo-hit stale=true at same timestamp as orchestrator commit. Serving runtime logs show decision-conflict where edge bound variant != control-plane chosen variant.
Repro pattern: most reproducible when weight changes are applied within <2m of each other and when clients reconnect with reused keep-alive on multiplexed HTTP/2 streams.

Mitigation tried: targeted cache invalidation on affected edge shard reduced impact quickly. Hotfix added a reconciliation check in orchestrator to clear memo if cookie namespace/path semantics changed between snapshots.

Root cause likely multi-factor: (1) edge memoization TTL longer than snapshot reconciliation window, (2) cookie normalization change that altered matching semantics introduced a month ago, (3) orchestrator did not invalidate edge fingerprints when snapshot cookie metadata changed.
Monitoring added: added histogram of 'edge_conflict_rate' and alerting threshold at >2% conflict over 5m for any route during staged rollouts.
resolution: Mitigation: performed targeted edge shard cache invalidation which restored expected routing for DataStream Labs. Fix: rolled out PR to orchestrator (https://github.com/redwood-inference/orchestrator/pull/1267) that enforces cookie-scope and path normalization checks during snapshot commit and proactively emits invalidation signals to edge for affected shards. Follow-ups: INT-2201 to add e2e tests for cookie normalization across canary weight shifts, and a runbook update (Confluence link added). Customer communicated that metrics and quality returned to baseline; monitoring remains active for 72h. Ticket set to In Progress pending postmortem and closing notes.
